rubric: One element is clearly read first: the headline is much larger than the body text and nothing else competes with it.
There is exactly one primary call to action; the secondary link is visibly quieter than the button.
The paragraph under the headline has a comfortable line length (about 40 to 75 characters) and secondary text still has strong contrast against its background.
Spacing groups the headline, paragraph and buttons as one unit, with generous whitespace and consistent alignment of edges.
The product visual looks specific to an invoice-reminder tool and supports the message without competing with the headline.

result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): B's product visual is clean and fully contained: an invoice list, a reminder email preview and a 'paid' toast, all clearly about invoice reminders, with no truncation. A has a strong headline and good copy, but its visual runs off the right edge of the page. Names are truncated ('North Ha...', 'Meridian ...'), and the toast and email card are clipped, which makes it look broken. A also has a dark 'Start free' button in the nav that slightly competes with the main call to action. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): A is a clean, well-balanced hero: the headline clearly dominates, there's one strong button with a quieter underlined demo link, and the invoice list with a reminder email preview fits the product while sitting fully inside the frame. B's visual is clipped off the right and bottom edges, with truncated names, cramped wrapping and a cut-off toast. B's dark 'Start free' nav button also competes with the hero CTA, and its bold demo link is less clearly secondary.
